_readme: Themed puzzles. This file is the ONLY place a theme is authored — the
generator merges it over the generated set, so an editor never touches code.
A theme claims a base word. Claimed bases are generated FIRST and win their
anagram slot, so a claim reliably lands. Clues written here override the
auto-generated Webster ones; anything not overridden falls back, so a theme
Clue rules, enforced by the build (it prints what it rejected and why):
- never contain the answer or a 4+ character stem of it
- no two rows in a puzzle may pose the same question
VOICE NOTE: these are a first draft written to prove the pipeline and give
an editor something to react to. They should be revised by someone with
standing to write them. Warmth and specificity over slang-as-punchline.

themes.name: The Cookout
themes.blurb: Paper plates, folding chairs, somebody's uncle on the grill.

themes.name: 90s R&B
themes.blurb: Slow jams, harmonies, and a CD case in the car door.

themes.name: Sitcom Sunday
themes.blurb: Reruns, laugh tracks, and everybody's living room.

themes.name: HBCU
themes.blurb: The yard, the band, the homecoming.

themes.name: Barbershop
themes.blurb: The chair, the clippers, and the argument already in progress.

clues.cousin: The one at every function you can't quite chart on the family tree.
clues.coins: What the ice cream truck required, dug out of a car door.
clues.icons: The framed faces on the hallway wall, next to the graduation photos.
clues.cons: The drawbacks somebody lists before agreeing to host next year.
clues.ions: Charged particles — the science-fair topic that got picked twice.
clues.nous: Good sense; the thing the aunties have and say you're short on.

clues.vocals: The part you rewind for, isolated from everything else.
clues.coals: What's still glowing after everybody's eaten.
clues.cola: Dark, sweet, and poured over ice in a red cup.
clues.oval: The shape of a running track, or a serving platter.
clues.lac: A resinous substance from insects, used to make shellac.
clues.sal: In an old apothecary's Latin, the common white seasoning.

clues.sample: Four bars borrowed, looped, and turned into something else entirely.
clues.ample: More than enough — the amount of food your grandmother made.
clues.lapse: A slip, or a stretch of time quietly passing.
clues.leaps: Jumps — what a chorus does after a quiet verse.
clues.maple: A tree with winged seeds, and a syrup.
clues.pales: Grows lighter, or fades next to something stronger.

clues.sitcom: Half an hour, one living room, and everybody back to normal by the end.
clues.moist: Slightly damp — the word the whole internet agreed to hate.
clues.stoic: Unbothered on purpose. The dad on every one of these shows.
clues.mist: Fine spray hanging in the air, like over a cold drink in July.
clues.most: The greatest amount — what the middle child claims to do.
clues.its: Belonging to it. The apostrophe goes nowhere near this one.

clues.laughs: What the track supplies whether the joke earned it or not.
clues.gush: To pour out praise a little too enthusiastically.
clues.hags: Unkind word for old women; the villain in a fairy tale, retold.
clues.haul: To drag the folding table in from the garage.
clues.lash: To bind tight — or the strip that frames an eye.
clues.shag: A carpet deep enough to lose a remote in.

clues.campus: The yard. Where the band practices and everybody ends up walking.
clues.camps: Where the freshmen get sent before the first week starts.
clues.cams: Rotating parts that turn a spin into a push.
clues.cusp: Right on the edge of becoming something else.
clues.maps: What you don't need by October.
clues.scum: A film on the surface of standing water.

clues.alumni: The ones who graduated and still come back for the game.
clues.luna: Of the moon — also a big pale-green moth.
clues.mail: What used to bring the acceptance letter, in a thick envelope.
clues.mina: A talking bird of southern Asia, good at mimicry.
clues.nail: To hit something exactly right, the way a routine lands.
clues.ail: To trouble or make unwell; what's wrong when nothing specific is.

clues.chairs: Where you wait, and where the conversation actually happens.
clues.crash: To drop in without an appointment and hope for a gap.
clues.hairs: What ends up on the cape, and on the floor, and on your neck.
clues.airs: Putting them on: acting grander than anybody's buying.
clues.arch: A curve — also the shape of a very deliberate eyebrow.
clues.cars: What's double-parked outside for the whole afternoon.

clues.shaved: Taken down clean with a blade.
clues.hades: The underworld of Greek myth, ruled by a god of the same name.
clues.heads: What everybody in the shop turns when the door opens.
clues.shade: Cool relief from the sun — or a remark delivered very politely.
clues.dash: A quick run, or a small pour of something into the pan.
clues.have: To possess. As in: he does not the receipts.

clues.faucet: Where the water comes out, and where the dishes pile up under it.
clues.cafe: Somewhere you order coffee and stay two hours longer than planned.
clues.cute: What you call the little jug nobody is allowed to actually use.
clues.acute: Sharp — a pain, an angle, or a sense of smell near the stove.
clues.face: The front of a thing; what you put on before opening the door.
clues.fate: What you blame when the cake doesn't rise.
